claims.value: all and only 36 deposited RAW acquisitions
claims.evidence: The UTF-16 metadata table contains one exact filename match for each accession-scoped PRIDE RAW file.

claims.location: source name; characteristics[specimen identifier]; characteristics[archaeological site]
claims.value: depositor specimen, site, and extraction batch
claims.evidence: Naxian and Baxian sample IDs and sites are per-injection metadata values. Repeated Baxian S1/S2 acquisitions share preparation identifiers.

claims.value: depositor identified taxon with controlled broad organism where necessary
claims.evidence: The exact source identification is retained in taxonomic identification. Homo sp. is encoded as Homo. Stegodon lacks an accepted local NCBI taxonomy cache term, so Mammalia is used as a truthful broader controlled organism. Extraction blanks use not applicable.

claims.value: tooth enamel or dentin; per-run 10% TFA, 10% EDTA, 5% HCl, or 0.6 M HCl
claims.evidence: The metadata table supplies tissue and buffer for every run; the project protocol describes corresponding extraction workflows.

claims.value: Exploris 480 for Naxian; Fusion Lumos for Baxian
claims.evidence: Project sample-processing protocol assigns the Naxian fauna and hominin to Exploris 480 and Baxian enamel/dentine to Fusion Lumos; filename prefixes identify these groups.

claims.value: unspecific cleavage for enamel and its blanks; Trypsin for dentine and its extraction blanks
claims.evidence: Project protocol describes acid-extracted enamel without enzymatic digestion and in-solution trypsin digestion for faunal and Baxian hominin dentine. Blank workflow follows its labeled material type.

claims.value: S1 and S2 when explicitly named; otherwise 1
claims.evidence: The S1/S2 suffix distinguishes paired Baxian acquisitions of the same preparation.

limitations: The validator requires a numeric biological replicate for extraction blank rows; 1 denotes the first blank preparation, not a biological organism.
Project processing describes multiple search engines and nonuniform PTM settings; precise modification lists and mass tolerances are omitted rather than projected onto every run.
Stegodon is recorded exactly in taxonomic identification while characteristics[organism] uses the accepted broader Mammalia term.
